chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer is firmer/stronger than the mountain. The mountain loses its parts (is eroded), but no loss takes place in the religion of the believer.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of a believer being stronger than a mountain?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent narrator Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith employs the metaphor of a mountain to illustrate the spiritual resilience of the believer, emphasizing that while physical mountains may be eroded or diminished, the faith of a true mu'min remains impervious to external pressures. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia scholarship as a definition of 'istiqamah' (steadfastness), distinguishing the believer's internal fortitude from the transient nature of the material world. It serves as a practical benchmark for evaluating the depth of one's conviction during times of trial.
